answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on an attestation graph, so influence from honest roots decays with path length rather than spreading without limit. A sybil cluster attached through a sparse external cut has low conductance—the cut’s edge volume is small relative to the cluster’s degree volume—and min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore limit its reachable trust and aggregate voting weight, assuming bounded per-node influence. Labels such as garden, mesa, and copper do not alter that structural bound.
